headline: Executive order sets up a federal task force to enforce the ban on importing goods made with forced labor, under the USMCA trade law.
what_it_does: This order creates the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force, as called for in Section 741 of the law that put the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) into effect. The task force is meant to oversee how the U.S. enforces its ban on bringing in goods made with forced labor. Only the title is available, so details such as who sits on the task force and its specific duties are not covered here.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that handle trade and imports
who_it_affects.how: Officials from these agencies would work together on the new task force to oversee forced labor import rules.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that import goods into the United States
who_it_affects.how: They could face closer checks on whether the goods they bring in were made with forced labor.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed May 15, 2020; executive orders generally take effect when signed.
